messages.text:
Trestle proposes a **$186,000 base salary and a $15,000 signing bonus for a start by May 3, 2027**. That gives Mara time to take ownership of the internal security platform and lead its preparation for the July audit. If she can start by April 19, we can raise the signing bonus to **$18,000** at the same base.

For the first 12 weeks, we propose one site visit each week. If fewer trips work better for Mara, we can group that time into two three-day visits per month, with Trestle covering travel. We can also put business-hours-only incident coverage in writing. Trestle would designate the after-hours escalation partner, and Mara would train that person during business hours as part of onboarding.

Which start date and travel schedule can Mara recommend? If a different balance of base salary and signing bonus would bring the package together, please include it in your counterproposal.

June 1, 2027 is Mara’s earliest start. She proposes a **$195,000 base and a $12,000 signing bonus** to replace the vest she would forfeit by starting then. If Trestle prefers to forgo the bonus, she can start July 1 at the same base.

For the first 12 weeks, Mara can make **two three-day visits per month**, with Trestle covering travel. After onboarding, she proposes working remotely with any site visits grouped and scheduled by agreement, up to twice a month.

For a June 1 start, Mara can lead the platform’s preparation for the July audit. She’d like the offer to give her ongoing ownership of security architecture for the internal platform, including authority to set design standards and approve security designs. Who owns audit preparation until she starts, and which July deliverables would she inherit? If Trestle prefers July 1, we’d need to agree on a narrower audit handoff.

Business-hours-only incident coverage works for Mara. Before recommending acceptance, we’d need Trestle to identify the after-hours escalation partner and confirm who covers that person’s absences and the period while Mara trains them. Can Trestle confirm that staffing and include the coverage terms, architecture authority, travel schedule, and agreed compensation in the written offer?

Trestle can recommend a **June 1, 2027 start at a $190,000 annual base with a $17,000 signing bonus**, payable with Mara’s first paycheck. That matches the $207,000 in combined first-year base and signing pay in Mara’s June proposal and gives her June to prepare for the audit.

We propose the following terms for the written offer.

- **Architecture authority.** Mara will own security architecture for Trestle’s internal platform, set its security design standards, and have approval authority over platform security designs.
- **July audit.** Trestle proposes that the security engineering manager own platform audit preparation through May 31. On June 1, the manager will give Mara the audit scope, control owners, evidence collected to date, open gaps, and deadlines. Mara will lead the platform’s July deliverables: the evidence submission, a remediation plan for outstanding gaps with owners and dates, and responses to auditors’ platform questions. Control owners will remain responsible for producing their evidence and carrying out assigned fixes.
- **Travel.** During the first 12 weeks, Mara will make two three-day site visits per month, with Trestle covering travel expenses. Afterward, she will work remotely, with any site visits grouped, scheduled by mutual agreement, and limited to two visits per month. Trestle will cover those trips as well.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara’s incident duties will be limited to business hours from her first day, including training the escalation partner. Trestle will retain responsibility for after-hours coverage throughout training and whenever the partner is absent. The primary and backup assignments are still unconfirmed. Before asking Mara to accept, Trestle will identify both people in writing and specify who holds the pager on each shift until the trained partner takes over.

Subject to that written staffing confirmation, can you recommend the June 1 package at $190,000 base and $17,000 signing?

Yes. I can recommend the June 1, 2027 package to Mara at a **$190,000 annual base and a $17,000 signing bonus payable with her first paycheck**, once Trestle confirms after-hours staffing in writing.

The proposed architecture authority, June 1 audit handoff, July deliverables, grouped travel schedule, and business-hours-only incident duties work for Mara. Please include those terms in the offer. The remaining dependency is written confirmation naming the primary and backup responders and identifying who holds the pager on each after-hours shift during training and who covers absences afterward. With that confirmation and the offer as proposed, I can recommend acceptance.

Trestle will include the agreed terms in the written offer:

- **Start and compensation.** Mara will start June 1, 2027, at a $190,000 annual base salary. Trestle will pay the $17,000 signing bonus with her first paycheck.
- **Architecture authority.** Mara will own security architecture for the internal platform, set its security design standards, and approve platform security designs.
- **Audit handoff.** The security engineering manager will own platform audit preparation through May 31. On June 1, the manager will hand Mara the scope, control-owner list, evidence collected, open gaps, and deadlines. Mara will lead the July evidence submission, the remediation plan with owners and due dates, and responses to auditors’ platform questions. Control owners will produce their evidence and carry out assigned fixes.
- **Travel.** For the first 12 weeks, Mara will make two three-day site visits per month. Afterward, she will work remotely, with site visits grouped and scheduled by mutual agreement, up to twice per month. Trestle will cover travel expenses throughout.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara’s incident duties will be limited to business hours from her first day. She will train the escalation partner during business hours. Trestle will staff the after-hours pager throughout training and during responder absences.

**After-hours staffing is the sole open item.** Trestle has yet to confirm the responders’ names or shift assignments. Before requesting acceptance, Trestle will provide a written roster naming the primary and backup, identifying the pager holder for every after-hours shift during training, and specifying who takes the pager when the primary is absent after handoff.

If five consecutive days on site would help with the July audit, Mara can extend one planned July visit from three days to five, provided Trestle removes one earlier three-day trip. If Trestle prefers the agreed schedule, that still works. Please confirm which schedule you prefer and, for the five-day option, identify the audit dates and the trip it would replace.

Before I recommend acceptance, Mara needs two timing commitments in writing.

- **After-hours handover.** Please include the date and time the trained responder takes the pager, along with the agreed roster naming the primary, backup, and pager holder for each after-hours shift during training. If training runs past that date, please confirm who keeps the pager until handover. Mara will conduct training during business hours.
- **Travel reimbursement.** Mara proposes that Trestle reimburse travel expenses within 15 calendar days after she submits each expense report. If Trestle uses fixed payment dates, please specify those dates and the submission cutoff for each.

Trestle prefers the agreed schedule of **two three-day visits per month for the first 12 weeks**. We’d use the second June visit to cover the second site before the July audit. We propose June 8–10 at the primary site and June 22–24 at the second site. Both July visits would remain three days. Do those June dates and locations work for Mara?

**Travel reimbursement.** Trestle can include the 15-calendar-day reimbursement deadline in the offer, measured from submission of each expense report. We propose covering up to four hotel nights per visit. If Trestle’s itinerary or a travel disruption requires an additional night, Trestle will arrange and pay for it. Mara would pay for extra nights she adds for personal reasons. Can you recommend that arrangement?

**After-hours handover.** We propose June 25, 2027, at 5 p.m. in the primary site’s local time as the target for pager transfer. The transfer will occur only once training is complete and the trained responder acknowledges receipt. If training runs late, the scheduled after-hours pager holder will retain responsibility until the next rostered responder or the trained partner explicitly takes over. Mara will conduct training during business hours and will have no after-hours pager duty.

The responders’ names and shift assignments are still pending. Before requesting acceptance, Trestle will provide the written roster naming the primary and backup, the pager holder for each training-period after-hours shift, and the people covering delays and absences. We’ll include the confirmed handover date, time, and time zone with that roster.

June 8–10 at the primary site and June 22–24 at the second site work for Mara. Both July visits can remain three days.

I can recommend reimbursement within 15 calendar days of each expense report’s submission and coverage for up to four hotel nights per visit. Trestle will arrange and pay for any additional night its itinerary or a travel disruption requires. Mara will cover any extra nights she adds for personal reasons.

June 25, 2027 at 5 p.m. in the primary site’s local time works as the target handover. The scheduled responder retains the pager until another rostered responder explicitly takes over. The trained partner takes over once training is complete and they acknowledge receipt. Mara has no after-hours pager duty.

The remaining dependency is the written roster and handover confirmation. Once Trestle names the primary and backup, identifies who covers each after-hours shift during training and any delays or absences, and confirms the handover date, time, and time zone in writing, I can recommend acceptance of the June 1 package on the agreed terms.
